findings.title: All highscore and user-level traffic sent over cleartext HTTP
findings.code_excerpt:
public final static String USERLEVELS_GETPHP = "http://www.apo-games.de/apoClock4k/get_level.php";
public final static String HIGHSCORE_SAVEPHP = "http://www.apo-games.de/apoClock4k/save_highscore.php";
findings.entry_point: Network responses and requests of get_level.php / save_level.php / get_highscore.php / save_highscore.php (all four URLs defined at lines 5-9)
findings.data_path: UI action -> ApoClockPanel.loadUserlevels() (ApoClockPanel.java:139-147) or ApoClockArcarde.init() (ApoClockArcarde.java:39-46) -> ApoClockUserlevelsLoad.load()/save() / ApoClockHighscoreLoad.load()/save() -> new URL(<http constant>).openConnection(); server lines parsed into ArrayLists (names, levels, times) that populate in-game UI and ApoClockLevel.editorLevels (ApoClockUserlevels.java:30)
findings.attack_scenario: Attacker on the same LAN (open Wi-Fi, ARP spoofing) or any on-path position passively reads the player-chosen name and scores submitted in plaintext, and actively rewrites the get_level.php/get_highscore.php responses: injecting arbitrary level strings and highscore names that the client renders and plays without any origin check. This is also the remote delivery vector for ApoClock-03 payloads.
findings.preconditions: Device online (ApoClock.isOnline(), ApoClock.java:44-49); attacker positioned on-path or controlling DNS for www.apo-games.de. Note: apo-games.de may no longer resolve today; an attacker can still exploit via DNS spoofing to their own server.
findings.validation_plan: Run the app on an emulator whose DNS for www.apo-games.de points to a local mock host. Observe in tcpdump/mitmproxy that POST bodies containing 'name='/'level='/plaintext scores arrive unencrypted. Return crafted rows from the mock get_highscore.php (5-line groups) and get_level.php (11-line groups, see ApoClockHighscoreLoad.java:145-158 / ApoClockUserlevelsLoad.java:182-207) and verify the forged names/levels appear in the arcade highscore panel and the userlevels list.

findings.title: Score and level submissions carry no authentication or integrity protection
findings.code_excerpt:
String content = "points=" + URLEncoder.encode(String.valueOf(points), "UTF-8") + "&clocks=" + URLEncoder.encode(String.valueOf(clocks), "UTF-8") + "&name=" + URLEncoder.encode(name, "UTF-8");
printout.writeBytes(content);
findings.entry_point: Anyone able to send an HTTP POST; the game itself contributes only client-computed values (p[1]/clocks from ApoClockArcardeGame.think(), ApoClockArcarde.setPoints() at ApoClockArcarde.java:84-91)
findings.sink: POST body written to http://www.apo-games.de/apoClock4k/save_highscore.php (writeBytes at ApoClockHighscoreLoad.java:96); identically shaped upload of arbitrary level strings to save_level.php (ApoClockUserlevelsLoad.java:132-133)
findings.data_path: No token, session, signature, MD5 checksum, or server-side attestation exists anywhere in the request: the entire message is 'points=<int>&clocks=<int>&name=<string>' (lines 92-94). The same anonymous pattern uploads editor-built level strings via ApoClockEditor.uploadString() -> ApoClockUserlevels.addLevel() (ApoClockEditor.java:180-187, ApoClockUserlevels.java:81-88).
findings.attack_scenario: Step 1: attacker runs `curl -d 'points=999999&clocks=999&name=anyone' http://www.apo-games.de/apoClock4k/save_highscore.php` without ever playing; Step 2: every client calling load() renders the forged entry at the top of the online board (ApoClockHighscore.drawHighscore, ApoClockHighscore.java:81-99). The same one-liner seeds save_level.php with arbitrary strings, making the server a distribution channel for the malformed levels of ApoClock-03.
findings.preconditions: Endpoint reachable (original server or an attacker-operated clone reached via ApoClock-01's transport position). No credentials exist in the app to steal - submission is anonymous by design.
findings.validation_plan: Point the device/emulator at a mock endpoint (or hit the live URL if still up) with the curl command above; then press 'arcade' in-game and observe the forged name/points rendered in the online highscore list after load(). Repeat with save_level.php using level='240,260,40,-50,0' and confirm it appears in the userlevels chooser.

findings.entry_point: Level strings downloaded from get_level.php (cleartext, see ApoClock-01) or uploaded by any anonymous player via save_level.php (see ApoClock-02); stored in ApoClockLevel.editorLevels (ApoClockUserlevels.java:30)
findings.sink: Hand-rolled tokenizer loadLevelWithString() at ApoClockPuzzleGame.java:141-166 (l[y+4] indexing, Integer.valueOf) feeding the physics loop at lines 224-244 whose while-extraction depends entirely on the attacker-supplied velocity value
findings.data_path: ApoClockPuzzle.touchedButton(USERLEVELS) -> ApoClockPanel.setPuzzleGame(0,null,true) (no try/catch, ApoClockPanel.java:234-251) -> ApoClockPuzzleGame.loadLevel() -> loadLevelWithString(ApoClockLevel.editorLevels[curLevel]) (line 135). Three failure modes: (a) token count not a multiple of 5 -> ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException at l[y+4] (lines 148-152), uncaught on this path -> app crash; (b) non-numeric token -> NumberFormatException, uncaught -> crash; (c) velocity token '0' or negative (editor clamps to [3,18] at ApoClockEditorClockStats.java:118-131, but network levels bypass the editor entirely; Math.abs is applied only to startAngle, line 153) -> in think() the loop does curTime += delta (line 225) then curTime -= rotateVelocity (line 238), which never decreases curTime when velocity<=0 -> endless spin of the game/GL thread -> permanent freeze/ANR whenever that level runs.
findings.attack_scenario: Attacker uploads level '240,260,40,-50,0' through the normal editor-upload button (or injects it into the cleartext get_level.php response). Victim opens Puzzlemode -> Userlevels and starts the level; on first touch the app hangs forever in ApoClockPuzzleGame.think and Android shows an App-Not-Responding dialog; re-entering reproduces it. Variants '1,2,3' or 'a,b,c,d,e' hard-crash the process instead.
findings.preconditions: Victim plays a user level whose string the attacker controls (server-side authorship via ApoClock-02, or on-path rewrite via ApoClock-01). No privileges on the victim device required.
findings.validation_plan: Serve an 11-line group from a mock get_level.php whose level line is exactly '240,260,40,-50,0' (metadata lines any integers, see parser ApoClockUserlevelsLoad.java:182-207). Launch app, tap puzzle->userlevels->start, touch screen; observe ANR ('Application Not Responding') and capture the stack: main/GL thread parked inside the while at line 226. Then repeat with level line '1,2,3' (ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException) and 'x,y,z,w,v' (NumberFormatException), each killing the process with no dialog.

findings.title: Persisted local highscore/progress string parsed without guards: tampering unlocks all levels or permanently crashes startup
findings.code_excerpt:
next = curString.indexOf(";");
this.clocks.add(Integer.valueOf(curString.substring(0, next)));  // next == -1 possible -> substring(0,-1) throws
findings.entry_point: 'highscore' and 'solved' values in the MODE_PRIVATE SharedPreferences file ApoClockPref (written at ApoClockPanel.java:129-137; editable by root or an adb backup/restore of net.apogames.apoclock)
findings.sink: setHighscoreFromString() at ApoClockHighscoreLocal.java:53-74, invoked un-guarded from ApoClockPanel.loadPreferences() (ApoClockPanel.java:121-122), which runs inside init() (ApoClockPanel.java:104) at every app start; 'solved' int feeds ApoClockPuzzleChooser.setSolved() (ApoClockPuzzleChooser.java:65-78) which gates level selection
findings.data_path: XML pref value -> getString('highscore','') (ApoClockPanel.java:121) -> setHighscoreFromString: loop reads pairs p;c up to 5 times; if the value ends after an odd ';' group (e.g. '12;'), indexOf(';') returns -1 and substring(0,-1)/Integer.valueOf throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException/NumberFormatException with no catch on the call chain -> exception during init() -> instant crash on every launch (crash loop until prefs cleared). Separately, because the format is plaintext and unchecked, setting 'solved'=28 or 'highscore'=99999;1; grants all levels/top local score (client-side trust, no MAC/signature).
findings.attack_scenario: On a rooted device (or via adb backup/restore on builds that permit it): edit /data/data/net.apogames.apoclock/shared_prefs/ApoClockPref.xml, set solved=28 to unlock every puzzle level, or set highscore to '12;' - the latter bricks the app into a startup crash loop that survives restarts until the app's data is cleared.
findings.preconditions: Local attacker with root, or ability to backup/restore app data; SharedPreferences are otherwise app-private, so this is local-tamper/cheat tier, not remote.
findings.validation_plan: adb backup the app, unpack with abe, change the 'highscore' string to '12;' and restore; launch and observe immediate force-close with StringIndexOutOfBoundsException at ApoClockHighscoreLocal.java:69 (repeat-crash on relaunch). In a second run set solved=28 and observe all 28 level buttons unlocked/green in the chooser without solving anything.

notes: This is the smallest, cleanest variant audited shape-wise: an Android-only port (BitsApp/bits-engine) with no applet entry point. (1) remote_code_loading: grep found no ClassLoader/defineClass/System.load in game code; the only native hook is System.loadLibrary("modplug-"+VERS) in the VENDORED third-party tree (_from_jar_andmodplug.../PlayerThread.java:912), and no net.apogames class imports com.peculiargames or com.leff (verified by import scan) - the andmodplug/MIDI jars are dead copies here, so the JNI loader and their MOD/MIDI parsers are NOT reachable. (2) untrusted_deserialization: no ObjectInputStream/Serializable anywhere. (3) weak_integrity_check: no MessageDigest/MD5/hash at all in this variant (unlike some siblings); integrity absence is covered by ApoClock-02. (4) path_traversal: game code performs zero filesystem I/O - persistence is exclusively SharedPreferences (ApoClock.java:39); the .cheat/.mar/.skunk/.rep-style custom formats of other variants do not appear here; the custom formats that DO exist (level CSV at ApoClockPuzzleGame.java:141-166, 'p;c;p;c;' local highscore at ApoClockHighscoreLocal.java:53-74) are findings 03/04. (5) Minor, below finding threshold: Log.d prints player name+score to logcat (ApoClockHighscoreLoad.java:73,95; ApoClockHighscoreLocal.java:58,65,67; ApoClockPanel.java? none) - information_disclosure only via adb/root, negligible; NetworkInfo is cached once at onCreate (ApoClock.java:36-37) so isOnline() goes stale - robustness only; ApoClockHighscore.saveHighscore (ApoClockHighscore.java:64-79) reads bReturn before its upload thread finishes and indexes sortByHighscore.get(4) guarded only by points-size>5 - latent races, not attacker-facing. All real attack surface concentrates in the four anonymous HTTP endpoints and the two hand parsers that consume their output.
